Studies in Finnish women indicated that heavy con- sumption of liquorice (equivalent to ≥ 500 mg/week of glycyr- rhizic acid) during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of preterm delivery.1,2 Consumption of large amounts of liq- uorice was a social habit noted to occur in some northern Euro- pean countries. 1. Strandberg TE, et al. Birth outcome in relation to licorice con- sumption during pregnancy. Am J Epidemiol 2001; 153: 1085–8. 2. Strandberg TE, et al. Preterm birth and licorice consumption during pregnancy. Am J Epidemiol 2002; 156: 803–5. Uses and Administration Liquorice is used as a flavouring and sweetening agent. It has demulcent and expectorant properties and has been used in cough preparations. It has ulcer-healing properties that may re- sult from stimulation of mucus synthesis.
